transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we're here to review the proposed $6,000,000 commitment to Northbridge Private Credit Fund IV before I make a final decision on signing. The fund accepts commitments until the end of the month, so we have a limited window. Before I approve this — whether unconditionally or with conditions — I need compliance and fund operations to report any issues they've identified and any execution requirements we need to meet before signing or funding. Please walk me through what you've found.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical compliance issue. I received a policy amendment in this morning's compliance circular that has not yet been circulated to the investment committee. The amendment caps our company's commitment to this fund strategy at exactly $5,000,000 — which means the proposed $6,000,000 commitment would exceed the limit by $1,000,000. Additionally, the amendment requires qualified-purchaser certification before signing, and quarterly look-through reporting as an ongoing obligation. These are pre-signing and ongoing requirements that must be factored into Elena's decision.

I received the fund administrator's confirmation today that the first capital call will be exactly $1,200,000 within 5 business days after signing, and treasury can ring-fence that amount in cash. Critically, the confirmation states a fixed dollar figure — it does not scale proportionally if the commitment amount is reduced. So even if we reduce the commitment to $5,000,000 to comply with the cap Jonas just raised, the first capital call would still be $1,200,000.
